title: Acute Severe Dyspnea & Wheezing
learning_objectives: Screen for respiratory muscle fatigue and accessory muscle use
Administer back-to-back inhaled bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids

patient.name: Elena Rostova
patient.opening_statement: Doctor... I can't... breathe... Used my blue inhaler... four times... still tight...
patient.initial_statement: Doctor... I can't... breathe... Used my blue inhaler... four times... still tight...
patient.presentation_complaint: I can barely catch my breath... My inhaler isn't working.

chief_complaint.value: I started having severe trouble catching my breath, and my blue inhaler isn't working.

onset_activity.value: I was visiting a friend who has two cats.

character.value: It feels like breathing through a thin straw, with a tight band squeezing my chest.

severity.value: It's about an 8 out of 10 difficulty breathing.

radiation.value: No, it stays right where it is. It hasn't spread anywhere else.

timing.value: It hasn't really gone away and has gotten worse.

aggravating_factors.value: Any physical activity or breathing in cold air makes it much worse.

relieving_factors.value: My inhaler gave only about ten minutes of slight relief before the tightness came right back.

pertinent_negatives: No fever, chills, or purulent sputum
No leg swelling or prior DVT

past_medical_history: Moderate persistent asthma diagnosed at age 11
Cat dander and grass pollen allergy
One prior ICU admission for asthma at age 19
medications: Albuterol 90 mcg HFA inhaler as needed
family_history: Mother has asthma; Brother had severe eczema growing up.
social_history: Never smoked, denies vaping or illicit substances.

examination.name: Pulmonary Auscultation & Work of Breathing
examination.findingDescription: Markedly prolonged expiratory phase. High-pitched polyphonic expiratory wheezes throughout all lung fields. Supraclavicular and intercostal retractions present.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Severe diffuse bronchospasm with significant airflow limitation.

examination.name: Precordial Auscultation
examination.findingDescription: Tachycardic regular rhythm at 112 bpm. Normal S1/S2. No murmurs or gallops.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Sinus tachycardia secondary to respiratory distress and albuterol use.

investigations.name: Chest Radiograph (CXR)
investigations.result: Hyperinflation with flattened diaphragms; no focal consolidation or pneumothorax
investigations.interpretation: Hyperinflation consistent with acute air trapping.

immediate_actions: Inhaled Albuterol + Ipratropium bromide nebulization back-to-back x 3
Oral Prednisone 60 mg or IV Methylprednisolone 60 mg STAT
contraindicated_actions: Sedatives or anxiolytics (risk of respiratory depression)

red_flags: Inability to speak in full sentences
critical_actions: Deliver nebulized short-acting beta agonist + anticholinergic
